question: how healthy is this company?

profitability.reading: Profitability is sound at the operating line and thin at the gross line. Over the trailing four quarters gross margin is {ratios.profitability.gross_margin|pct}, operating margin {ratios.profitability.operating_margin|pct} and net margin {ratios.profitability.net_margin|pct}. Against its own history the operating margin sits above the three-year average of {earnings_versus_cash.history.operating_margin_three_year_average|pct}. For fiscal 2025 the operating margin was {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.operating_margin|pct}. Gross margin is the weak leg: the quarter's {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.gross_margin|pct} is the second lowest of the six filled quarters, down from {trend_table.quarters-back-1.ratios.gross_margin|pct} the quarter before though above the year-ago quarter's {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.gross_margin|pct}. Fiscal 2025's {trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.gross_margin|pct} was the second lowest of five filled years, below fiscal 2023's {trend_table.years-back-2.ratios.gross_margin|pct}. Operating margin has widened because selling, general and administrative expense rose only modestly while revenue rose sharply, so the margin gain comes from scale rather than pricing. Net margin sits slightly above operating margin because of interest and other income, a currency gain and a low effective tax rate of {tax_rate|pct}. That support is soft: the MD&A puts lower interest income on "a decrease in average cash balance and short-term investment and a decrease of weighted average interest income rate", and the quarter's currency gain rests mainly on "unrealized gain from revaluation of outstanding Thai baht assets and liabilities of $12.7 million". Returns are high: return on assets is {ratios.profitability.return_on_assets|pct}, return on equity {ratios.profitability.return_on_equity|pct} and return on invested capital {ratios.profitability.return_on_invested_capital|pct}. The last is high partly because invested capital of {ratios.profitability.return_on_invested_capital.invested_capital} nets out the cash and short-term investments.

efficiency.reading: Working capital is where growth is costing the company. Over the trailing four quarters, on average balances, days sales outstanding are {ratios.efficiency.days_sales_outstanding}, days sales of inventory {ratios.efficiency.days_sales_of_inventory} and days payables outstanding {ratios.efficiency.days_payables_outstanding}, for a cash conversion cycle of {ratios.efficiency.cash_conversion_cycle} days. Asset turnover is {ratios.efficiency.asset_turnover}. Inventory is the stretched account: the quarter's inventory days of {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.days_sales_of_inventory} are the second highest of the six filled quarters and well above the year-ago quarter's {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.days_sales_of_inventory}. Fiscal 2025's {trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.days_sales_of_inventory} was already up on fiscal 2024's {trend_table.years-back-1.ratios.days_sales_of_inventory}. Inventory rose by {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.inventory.balance_sheet_change} in a year, a sum equal to {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.inventory.share_of_net_income|pct} of trailing net income, and management attributes it to "an increase in inventories to support higher demand in the next quarter". Receivables rose by {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.balance_sheet_change}, and the quarter's collection days of {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.days_sales_outstanding} are up on the prior quarter's {trend_table.quarters-back-1.ratios.days_sales_outstanding} though a touch below the year-ago {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.days_sales_outstanding}. Management cites only "an increase in trade receivables due to timing of collection", while the allowance against receivables stands at {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.bad_debt_reserve_ratio|pct}, the lowest of the six filled quarters. Supplier credit carried much of the load: payables rose by {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.accounts_payable.balance_sheet_change}, described as "aligned with the increasing volume of inventories". Even so, trade working capital rose from {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_to_firm.trade_working_capital.a_year_earlier} to {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_to_firm.trade_working_capital.now}. The calculator carries no year-earlier cash conversion cycle or asset turnover, so their movement is read from the quarterly trend cells, not from a computed change.

liquidity.reading: Liquidity is strong. The current ratio is {ratios.liquidity.current_ratio} and the quick ratio {ratios.liquidity.quick_ratio}, with cash and short-term investments of {terms.cash_and_short_term_investments_now} against current liabilities of {terms.balances_now.current_liabilities}. No cash runway is computed because free cash flow over the trailing four quarters is not negative, so the company is not burning cash. The strain shows in the trend, not the level. Cash and short-term investments are about where they stood a year earlier, at {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_to_firm.net_working_capital_broad_not_used.a_year_earlier.inputs.cash_and_short_term_investments}, while current liabilities rose from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.current_liabilities}. Short-term investments fell from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.short_term_investments} to {terms.balances_now.short_term_investments}, and the MD&A says lower investing outflow "was primarily due to an increase in net proceeds of short-term investments". Commitments outside the balance sheet are large: the notes state "purchase obligations and other commitments to third parties of $2.74 billion", which the notes reader describes as mainly inventory commitments, generally cancellable or reschedulable before delivery, and "total capital expenditure commitments to third parties of $164.7 million". After quarter end, cash leaves for the Raytek stake, bought "for approximately NT$1.02 billion ($32.4 million), subject to customary closing conditions". Against that, the credit facility is undrawn, and the MD&A states "cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments of $945.2 million and $950.7 million, respectively, and no outstanding debt". Customer advances also help: current contract liabilities rose from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.contract_liabilities} to {terms.balances_now.contract_liabilities}.

solvency.reading: Solvency is not a concern. Total debt is {ratios.solvency.total_debt}, because no current or non-current debt line is on record. Net debt is {ratios.solvency.net_debt}, a net cash position, and debt over EBITDA is {ratios.solvency.debt_over_ebitda} against trailing EBITDA of {ratios.solvency.ebitda}. Interest coverage is not in the calculator: no interest expense row exists for the year to date, which fits a company with nothing borrowed, and interest paid is likewise missing. Liabilities over assets is {ratios.solvency.liabilities_over_assets|pct}, and the operating lease liability is only {ratios.solvency.operating_lease_liability}. What has changed is the kind of liability carrying the balance sheet. Total liabilities rose from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.total_liabilities} to {terms.balances_now.total_liabilities}, led by trade payables of {terms.balances_now.accounts_payable} and by customer advances, not by borrowing. That is supplier and customer funding, which can reverse, but it is not leverage in the debt sense.

growth.reading: Growth is strong and accelerating in revenue and earnings, and negative in operating cash. Revenue grew {ratios.growth.revenue.quarter_over_quarter|pct} on the prior quarter, {ratios.growth.revenue.year_over_year|pct} on the year-ago quarter and {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct} over the trailing four quarters. That outpaces the company's own record. Fiscal 2025 revenue growth was {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.revenue_growth|pct}. The three-year compound rate is {earnings_versus_cash.history.revenue_growth_three_year_compound|pct} and the five-year rate {earnings_versus_cash.history.revenue_growth_five_year_compound|pct}. Operating income grew {ratios.growth.operating_income.quarter_over_quarter|pct}, {ratios.growth.operating_income.year_over_year|pct} and {ratios.growth.operating_income.trailing_four_quarters|pct} on the same three bases, and net income {ratios.growth.net_income.quarter_over_quarter|pct}, {ratios.growth.net_income.year_over_year|pct} and {ratios.growth.net_income.trailing_four_quarters|pct}. Operating cash flow went the other way. It rose {ratios.growth.operating_cash_flow.quarter_over_quarter|pct} on a weak prior quarter, but its change on the year-ago quarter is {ratios.growth.operating_cash_flow.year_over_year|pct} and over the trailing four quarters {ratios.growth.operating_cash_flow.trailing_four_quarters|pct}, both declines. Within revenue, growth leans on fewer and larger customers, the segment note saying "the Company had four and two customers, respectively, that each contributed 10% or more", while automotive fell in the quarter and data communication fell over nine months. No earnings release or outside expectation is in the record, so results against expectations cannot be read; the one item in that area reports revenue growth credited to key customers' demand.

free_cash_flow.reading: All four free cash flow measures are computed, so none is missing. Simple free cash flow over the trailing four quarters is {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_simple}, operating cash flow of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.operating_cash_flow} less capital spending of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.capital_expenditure}. Against the company's own history that is a sharp fall. Fiscal 2025 simple free cash flow was {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.free_cash_flow_simple}. Fiscal 2024 simple free cash flow was {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.free_cash_flow_simple}. Free cash flow to the firm is negative at {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_to_firm}, because after-tax operating profit is consumed by capital spending and by a rise in trade working capital of {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_to_firm.inputs.change_in_trade_working_capital}. Free cash flow to equity equals the simple measure at {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_to_equity}, since net borrowing is {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_to_equity.net_borrowing}. Quality-adjusted free cash flow is {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted} after deducting share-based compensation of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_based_compensation}; acquisitions are {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted.inputs.acquisitions.cash_spent}, and no other adjustment was applied or refused. Cash conversion of earnings has weakened: operating cash flow over net income is {earnings_versus_cash.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income} on a trailing basis. In fiscal 2025 the same ratio was {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income}. In fiscal 2024 it was {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income}. Accruals over average assets are {earnings_versus_cash.accruals_over_average_assets|pct}, and in the latest quarter operating cash flow of {ratios.growth.operating_cash_flow.this_quarter} compares with net income of {ratios.growth.net_income.this_quarter}. Smoothness is {earnings_versus_cash.smoothness}, below one, so reported income has moved far less than operating cash from quarter to quarter. Capital spending is up from {terms.trailing_four_quarters_a_year_earlier.capital_expenditure} a year earlier, against depreciation and amortization of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.depreciation_and_amortization}, for "the construction of a new manufacturing building at our Chonburi campus and support certain customers". Share repurchases over the trailing four quarters fell to {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_repurchases}, and the MD&A says lower financing outflow was "primarily due to a decrease in share repurchases". Dividends paid over the trailing four quarters are not in the calculator, because no row exists for the prior fiscal year.

dupont.reading: Return on equity of {ratios.profitability.dupont.product|pct} is net margin {ratios.profitability.dupont.net_margin|pct} times asset turnover {ratios.profitability.dupont.asset_turnover} times equity multiplier {ratios.profitability.dupont.equity_multiplier}. Asset turnover carries it: the margin is thin, as it is for a contract manufacturer, and the company turns its asset base more than once a year. The equity multiplier is modest and contains no borrowing, since total debt is {ratios.solvency.total_debt}; it is made of supplier payables, customer advances and other operating liabilities. The calculator holds no year-earlier decomposition, so the movement cannot be read from a computed field. The inputs give the direction only loosely. Trailing net income grew {ratios.growth.net_income.trailing_four_quarters|pct} against revenue's {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct}, so the margin leg did not widen. Liabilities grew from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.total_liabilities} to {terms.balances_now.total_liabilities} on payables and advances, which pushes the multiplier up. Return on equity is therefore being held up by turnover and by operating credit, not by better margins.

anomalies.what: With total debt of {ratios.solvency.total_debt}, solvency in the borrowing sense is under no pressure. The exposure is in what carries the balance sheet. Total liabilities rose from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.total_liabilities} to {terms.balances_now.total_liabilities}, and liabilities over assets is {ratios.solvency.liabilities_over_assets|pct}. Trade payables rose by {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.accounts_payable.balance_sheet_change}, "aligned with the increasing volume of inventories", and current contract liabilities rose from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.contract_liabilities} to {terms.balances_now.contract_liabilities}. Supplier credit and customer advances can be withdrawn faster than term debt, so if either reverses the cash would have to come from the liquid reserve.

path_to_distress.reading: The company is far from distress: it has no debt, a net cash position equal to its whole liquid reserve, and positive free cash flow. Distress would need several of the following to happen together. First, operating cash flow would have to keep falling while capital spending stays high, until simple free cash flow, now {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_simple}, turns negative. Only then would the calculator compute a cash runway, against cash and short-term investments of {terms.cash_and_short_term_investments_now}. Second, the inventory bought for "higher demand in the next quarter" would have to go unsold, pushing inventory days above the quarter's {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.days_sales_of_inventory} while the notes' "purchase obligations and other commitments to third parties of $2.74 billion" turn into cash calls. Third, suppliers or customers would have to pull back the credit that now funds working capital, shortening payables days from {ratios.efficiency.days_payables_outstanding} or drawing down customer advances of {terms.balances_now.contract_liabilities}. Fourth, a customer that contributes a tenth or more of revenue would have to leave or stop paying, with receivables of {terms.balances_now.receivables} concentrated in three of them. The point where liquidity itself would bend is the quick ratio, now {ratios.liquidity.quick_ratio}, falling toward one as current liabilities of {terms.balances_now.current_liabilities} outrun cash and receivables. Only after that would the company need to borrow. Debt maturing inside a year is {terms.debt_now.parts.debt_current}, interest coverage cannot be computed because no interest expense is on record, and net debt of {ratios.solvency.net_debt} would have to turn positive before leverage could become the problem.
